This year can be said to be the first year of super apps. OpenAI recently launched its own super app, but immediately admitted that the app "has some chaos." Now the CEO of Microsoft has also confirmed that a Copilot super app is about to be released.

Microsoft Copilot "Super App" will integrate diverse functions such as Cowork, chat, and coding

Microsoft is developing an AI "super app" that integrates Copilot's chat, coding, and agentic functions. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said on Wednesday's earnings call that this app will be launched this year, covering "consumer and business experiences." Nadella pointed out: "Copilot is rapidly evolving from chat to Cowork, and further developing into Autopilot." "This quarter, we will integrate these Copilot experiences—including coding functions—within the same super app……This is a significant step, and I look forward to sharing more details with everyone later."

OpenAI's own "super app" has already evolved into a mess, but that obviously has not stopped other companies from following this super app route.

Perhaps Microsoft can deliver a full-featured app more successfully and avoid repeating OpenAI's mistakes.

That said, CEO Satya Nadella also previously said that the company is gradually shifting away from apps and focusing on developing agents. The AI era is still emerging, and design trends and best practices surrounding AI interfaces are constantly changing.

As for Apple, there is no indication so far that it will move toward the super app direction; instead, it continues to launch independent and specialized new apps. Whether this strategy will change in the future remains to be seen.

What are your thoughts on the recent "super app" craze? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
